BiblicalUsage: zâʻêph means angry. In 1 Kings 20:43 we read, "And the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria." It appears again in 1 Kings 21:4: "And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him..."
TheologicalSignificance: za'eph is angry, and my position is that the plain words matter as much as the great ones, because God gave them all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
